sections.h2: What does the Madison County Clerk record?
sections.html:
The Madison County Clerk's Recordings Department files deeds, mortgages, wills, plats and other property papers for Madison County, Kentucky. Recordings are handled at the Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave., Richmond, KY 40475, which is open 8 AM to 4:30 PM. The recordings line is (859) 624-4703, extension 3.

The Berea Branch at 304 Chestnut St. lists motor vehicle work, dealer work, marriage licenses, voter registration and delinquent tax payments, but recordings are listed only for Richmond. If the clerk's website shows a relocation notice for the Richmond branch, confirm the address by phone before you drive over with a deed.

Electronic filings are processed daily until about 9:30 to 10:00 AM, and no wait-ons are available during that window. The clerk's records date back to 1786, and documents from 1986 forward are scanned. They can be viewed in person or online through ECCLIX, a third-party subscription service, and every search is by a person's name, not by street address.

sections.h2: What must a Kentucky deed include before the clerk will accept it?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 lists the required contents, and the statute bars a clerk from lodging a deed that does not comply. A seller who hands the closing agent accurate names and addresses saves a rejected filing.

  • The full names of grantor and grantee.
  • The mailing addresses of both.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in-care-of address where the current year's property tax bill may be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate, signed by both sides, that the stated price is the full price paid. For a gift or nominal price, the certificate states that the transfer is a gift and gives the estimated fair cash value.

Some deeds skip the consideration items, including deeds that convey only a utility easement, divorce transfers made by court action, deeds that correct an earlier error between the same parties, and cemetery lots. In a swap of properties, each property's fair cash value must be stated in the body of the deed.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record documents in Madison County?
sections.html:
Recording fees follow a posted schedule that combines a recording fee, an affordable housing trust fund charge and a state clerk fee. The schedule the clerk posts is dated 2020, and the amounts below come from it. Call the Recordings Department to confirm current charges before you send a check.

Madison County Clerk recording fees from the posted 2020 fee schedule
DocumentTotal feePage note
Deed$50.00Add $3.00 per page after 5
Mortgage$80.00Add $3.00 per page after 30
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46.00Add $3.00 per page after 5
Affidavit of descent$50.00Add $3.00 per page after 5
Power of attorney$50.00Add $3.00 per page after 5
Will$47.00Add $3.00 per page after 5
Certified copy$5.00Plus 50 cents a page after 3 pages

The schedule also notes an extra $4.00 for each additional reference on a document and a $7.00 charge for each notarization, so a closing package with several parcels costs more than one with a single legal description. The clerk's notary service is available only for documents being recorded in that office.

sections.h2: How is the Kentucky real estate transfer tax figured?
sections.html:
The tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, imposed on the grantor named in the deed. KRS 142.050 tells the county clerk to compute the amount and collect it before accepting the deed, and the clerk certifies the payment date and amount on the document.

Value means the full consideration, including liens, for a sale. For a gift or a deed with only nominal consideration, it means the estimated open-market price. To see the math, take the county's $232,000 median owner-occupied home value from the Census Bureau: $232,000 divided by $500 is 464, so the tax is $232.00. A sale at $232,100 adds one more unit and the tax becomes $232.50. The clerk keeps 5 percent of what it collects as a fee and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months.

  • Exempt transfers include transfers under a foreclosure or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Also exempt: transfers between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, partition transfers, and sales for delinquent taxes.
  • Transfers between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild with only nominal consideration are exempt.

sections.h2: How are inherited homes recorded in Madison County?
sections.html:
A will is recorded by presenting the original with the court order attached. The clerk keeps the original and charges the Will fee on its posted schedule. When someone dies without a will, an affidavit of descent under KRS 382.120 goes on record.

The statute also tells the personal representative of an estate to file an affidavit with the county clerk of each county where property lies, before closing out the estate. It lists the people receiving each property and the full or estimated market value of each. Heirs who plan to sell should ask the probate attorney whether that affidavit is on file, because a buyer's title examiner will look for it.

The clerk also offers DocAlert, a free service that emails you when a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name. It matches exact names only, so trusts and businesses should sign up under each spelling variation.

sections.h2: Where do delinquent Madison County property taxes go?
sections.html:
The Madison County Sheriff takes the first payment, and the County Clerk takes over after the bill goes delinquent. The Sheriff's Office is at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, with phone 859-623-1511 and hours Monday through Friday from 8:00 to 4:30. Do not mail cash.

After the bill moves, the clerk's Delinquent Taxes page (extension 2 on the Richmond line) lists the sale rules. The 2026 sale date for the 2025 bills was set for Thursday, August 27, at 9 AM in the Fiscal Courtroom of the Courthouse Annex, 135 W. Irvine St. State law requires advertising 30 to 45 days before. Buyers who want a bill register, pay $250, and put down a 25 percent deposit ten days ahead, using certified funds. A buyer's recording fees on the lien are $30 for an assignment and $46 for a release.

The county tax is split among the library, fiscal court, EMS, health department, school board and extension office, plus the Red Lick watershed, the City of Richmond, the City of Berea and the Berea Independent School District where they apply.

sections.h2: What should a Madison County seller know about the local market?
sections.html:
Madison County is growing fast. The Census Bureau estimates 101,696 residents for 2025, up 9.7 percent since April 2020, and 62 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied value is $232,000, median gross rent is $889, and 34.4 percent of adults age 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

Richmond, founded in 1798, is the seat and home of Eastern Kentucky University, and Berea hosts Berea College. I-75, U.S. 25 and U.S. 421 serve the county, and downtown Lexington is about 25 miles northwest of Richmond by I-75. Daniel Boone's Fort Boonesborough, now a state historic site, anchors local history. The county was formed in 1785 from part of Lincoln County.

Closing agents usually record the deed the day of closing, so ask early for the clerk's current fees and a transfer-tax figure for your price.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Madison County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: Record it at the Madison County Clerk's Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave., Richmond. The recordings line is (859) 624-4703, extension 3, and the office is open 8 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Madison County home sale?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value, or a fraction of $500. A $232,000 sale produces $232.00, and the clerk collects it before accepting the deed.

faqs.q: Does a Kentucky deed need a notarized price statement?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 382.135 requires a sworn, notarized certificate signed by grantor and grantee that the price in the deed is the full consideration paid. For a gift, the certificate says so and states the estimated fair cash value.

faqs.q: Can I search Madison County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes, through ECCLIX, a third-party subscription service, though every record is searchable by a person's name only. Documents from 1986 forward are scanned, and older records are viewed in the Richmond office.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Madison County property tax?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the County Clerk after the Sheriff's collection period, gains a lien, and can be sold at the clerk's annual tax sale. Call the clerk's Richmond line, extension 2, for a payoff amount before the sale.
